source_chapter: 02 Development Program Foundation; 03 Four Main Areas of Soccer Development; 07 Training Methodology
progression_rule: Keep the work blocked and predictable until at least 80% of repetitions are clean in two sessions. Then progress from static to moving, variable, random, and time-limited execution without sacrificing technique.

exercises.name: Dynamic Movement Preparation
exercises.intensity_cue: Easy to moderate pacing
exercises.form_cue: Stay tall through the trunk and control each landing before changing direction.

exercises.name: Two-Foot Ball Manipulation
exercises.intensity_cue: Controlled speed with no more than two errors per set
exercises.form_cue: Use both feet and keep the ball within one step of the body.

exercises.name: Blocked Wall Passing
exercises.reps_or_duration: 25 passes per foot with 45 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Firm ground passes at 70% effort
exercises.form_cue: Plant beside the ball and point the standing foot toward the target.

exercises.name: First-Touch Gate Receiving
exercises.reps_or_duration: 8 receptions each side with 45 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: One controlled first touch through the gate
exercises.form_cue: Open the hips before contact and guide the ball into playable space.

exercises.name: Ball Coordination Challenge
exercises.intensity_cue: Smooth continuous contacts
exercises.form_cue: Keep the ankles active and make small adjustments under the center of mass.

target_goal: Perception, First Touch, and Passing Accuracy
progression_rule: Begin with a known target and unlimited touches. After two sessions at 80% passing accuracy, add random visual calls, reduce space, and progress from two-touch to one-touch play.

exercises.name: Pre-Reception Shoulder Check
exercises.intensity_cue: Complete two shoulder checks during the 3 seconds before each reception
exercises.form_cue: Move the eyes and head early, then return the eyes to the ball before contact.

exercises.name: Open-Body Back-Foot Receive
exercises.reps_or_duration: 10 receptions each side with 45 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: 80% accurate first touches into the next action
exercises.form_cue: Show the chest toward attacking depth and receive across the body with the back foot.

exercises.name: One-Two Touch Wall Passing
exercises.intensity_cue: Firm ground pass with one or two touches
exercises.form_cue: Pass with the foot farther from imagined pressure and keep the first touch out of the feet.

exercises.name: Random Color First Touch
exercises.intensity_cue: React to a parent, partner, or audio color call
exercises.form_cue: Scan before the ball arrives and take the first touch toward the called gate.

source_chapter: 03 Four Main Areas of Soccer Development; 05 Principles & Demands
progression_rule: Progress from a cone defender to passive pressure and then live pressure. Increase speed or reduce space only when the player can exit under control with both feet on at least 8 of 10 attempts.

exercises.name: Check-Away Check-To Movement
exercises.reps_or_duration: 8 repetitions each direction with 45 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Sharp 3-step separation before receiving
exercises.form_cue: Change direction with the hips low and arrive side-on to see the field.

exercises.name: Cone Defender Change of Rhythm
exercises.reps_or_duration: 6 attacks per foot with 60 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Slow approach followed by an explosive exit
exercises.form_cue: Attack the defender's front foot and push the exit touch beyond tackling range.

exercises.name: Two-Foot 1v1 Exit
exercises.reps_or_duration: 6 repetitions each side with 60 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Game speed with a clean exit through the gate
exercises.form_cue: Sell the feint with the shoulders and accelerate immediately after the touch.

exercises.name: Penetration and Finish
exercises.reps_or_duration: 8 finishes alternating feet with 60 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Controlled first touch followed by a decisive strike
exercises.form_cue: Move the defender first, then strike through the center of the ball with the head steady.

target_goal: Defensive Transition, Deceleration, and Recovery Speed
source_chapter: 03 Four Main Areas of Soccer Development; 05 Principles & Demands
progression_rule: Start from a planned turnover cue, then make the cue random. Add distance or an active ball carrier only while the player can close under control and maintain correct delay-and-direct positioning.

exercises.name: Turnover Reaction Sprint
exercises.intensity_cue: Explosive first three steps
exercises.form_cue: Turn from the hips, drive the arms, and attack the space immediately after the loss cue.

exercises.name: Close and Decelerate
exercises.intensity_cue: Fast approach, controlled final 2 meters
exercises.form_cue: Shorten the steps on arrival and keep the chest over the knees.

exercises.name: Delay and Direct Shadow
exercises.intensity_cue: Moderate movement with no crossed feet
exercises.form_cue: Stay side-on and curve the approach to show play toward the chosen side.

exercises.name: Recovery Run to Goal Side
exercises.intensity_cue: 90% sprint effort with full recovery
exercises.form_cue: Recover inside the ball line before turning to face the next action.

source_chapter: 02 Development Program Foundation; 06 Ages & Stages; 09 Player Selection Criteria
progression_rule: Keep repetitions short and provide full recovery so speed quality stays high. Add one repetition or a reaction cue only when times remain within 5% of the player's best effort; stop the speed block when quality falls outside that range.

exercises.name: Running and Skipping Mechanics
exercises.reps_or_duration: 20 meters per pattern with 30 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Easy rhythm progressing to moderate speed
exercises.form_cue: Keep the hips tall and place the foot beneath the body.

exercises.name: Reaction Acceleration
exercises.intensity_cue: 95% effort from a random visual or sound cue
exercises.form_cue: Lean from the ankles and push the ground behind the body.

exercises.name: Ten-Meter Sprint
exercises.intensity_cue: Maximum quality with no conditioning fatigue
exercises.form_cue: Drive through the first five steps before rising gradually.

exercises.name: Reactive Change of Direction
exercises.reps_or_duration: 2 repetitions each direction with 60 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Fast but balanced reaction to a color or direction call
exercises.form_cue: Lower the center of mass before the cut and push away from the outside leg.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Stick Landing
exercises.reps_or_duration: 6 repetitions per leg with 45 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Hold every landing for 2 seconds
exercises.form_cue: Keep the knee aligned over the middle toes and the pelvis level.

target_goal: Ball Mastery, Fun, and Early Decision-Making
progression_rule: Keep each activity brief and change tasks before concentration drops. Move from isolated skill to an eased decision task and then a scored challenge; progress through success and enjoyment rather than fatigue.

exercises.name: Ball-Based Warm-Up
exercises.intensity_cue: Easy playful pacing
exercises.form_cue: Use many small touches while keeping the head up between contacts.

exercises.name: Two-Foot Ball Mastery
exercises.intensity_cue: Controlled repetitions with both feet
exercises.form_cue: Keep the knees soft and move around the ball instead of reaching.

exercises.name: Wall Pass and Receive
exercises.intensity_cue: Accurate ground passes before adding speed
exercises.form_cue: Receive away from the body and prepare the next pass with the first touch.

exercises.name: Called-Gate Dribble
exercises.intensity_cue: React to a parent or audio cue
exercises.form_cue: Look up before choosing the gate and accelerate after changing direction.

exercises.name: Personal Best Finishing Game
exercises.intensity_cue: Score accuracy before power
exercises.form_cue: Place the non-kicking foot beside the ball and finish balanced.

target_goal: Technique Under Eased Pressure and Injury-Resistant Movement
source_chapter: 06 Ages & Stages; 07 Training Methodology; 08 Periodization of Te-Ta
progression_rule: Use the sequence warm-up, coordination, isolated technique, eased decision-making, and competitive challenge. Reduce touches or space only after clean movement and at least 80% technical success; do not use high-lactate conditioning as the progression.

exercises.name: Dynamic Mobility and Landing Prep
exercises.intensity_cue: Easy to moderate pacing
exercises.form_cue: Control trunk position and align the hip, knee, and foot on every landing.

exercises.name: Coordination With Ball
exercises.intensity_cue: Continuous quality touches
exercises.form_cue: Alternate feet and maintain balance while changing movement patterns.

exercises.name: Isolated Passing Pattern
exercises.intensity_cue: 80% accurate firm passes
exercises.form_cue: Scan, open the body, and play the next pass from the first touch.

exercises.name: Eased Random-Call Receiving
exercises.intensity_cue: Two-touch limit with random direction calls
exercises.form_cue: Recognize the cue before contact and receive away from pressure.

exercises.name: Competitive Accuracy Challenge
exercises.intensity_cue: Score one point for each clean action under the time limit
exercises.form_cue: Keep technique stable while decision speed increases.

exercises.name: Cooldown Mobility
exercises.intensity_cue: Very easy pacing
exercises.form_cue: Breathe slowly and move only through comfortable ranges.

target_goal: Game-Speed Technique, Strength, and Situational Decision-Making
source_chapter: 06 Ages & Stages; 07 Training Methodology; 08 Periodization of Te-Ta
progression_rule: Progress from dynamic isolated repetitions to random, time-and-space-limited work and finally active pressure. Increase complexity before volume and retain full recovery for maximal-speed actions.

exercises.name: Dynamic Warm-Up and SAQ
exercises.intensity_cue: Build from 60% to 85% effort
exercises.form_cue: Maintain strong posture and finish every direction change under control.

exercises.name: One-Touch Passing Speed
exercises.intensity_cue: Fast ball speed with at least 85% accuracy
exercises.form_cue: Prepare the hips before the ball arrives and meet the middle of the ball.

exercises.name: Random First-Touch Escape
exercises.intensity_cue: React to unpredictable pressure or direction cues
exercises.form_cue: Scan early and take the first touch beyond the pressure line.

exercises.name: Live 1v1 or Shadow Pressure
exercises.intensity_cue: Game speed with complete recovery
exercises.form_cue: Change rhythm after fixing the defender and protect the ball through contact.

exercises.name: Sprint to Finish
exercises.reps_or_duration: 10-meter sprint plus 1 shot with 75 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: 90-95% sprint effort and match-quality finish
exercises.form_cue: Regain balance with a preparation step before striking.

exercises.name: Cooldown and Session Review
exercises.intensity_cue: Very easy movement followed by a 1-10 session RPE
exercises.form_cue: Lower breathing rate, then record one successful action and one next focus.

source_chapter: 03 Four Main Areas of Soccer Development; 06 Ages & Stages; 07 Training Methodology
progression_rule: The parent begins as a server and cue giver, then adds passive and finally active pressure. Ask the player to explain the decision after each set; add difficulty only when the player identifies the cue and executes the chosen action consistently.

exercises.name: Parent Serve and Open Receive
exercises.reps_or_duration: 10 serves each side with 45 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Accurate service with unlimited touches first
exercises.form_cue: The player checks both shoulders and opens the body before the serve arrives.

exercises.name: Color Call First Touch
exercises.reps_or_duration: 8 calls each side with 45 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Random call after the ball starts moving
exercises.form_cue: The first touch must enter the called gate without crossing the feet.

exercises.name: Passive Defender Escape
exercises.reps_or_duration: 6 repetitions each foot with 60 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Parent applies 40-50% pressure
exercises.form_cue: Place the body between defender and ball, then exit into open space.

exercises.name: Live Choice Challenge
exercises.intensity_cue: Parent varies the pressure side at game speed
exercises.form_cue: The player scans, names the open option, and commits to the decision.

exercises.name: Player Self-Evaluation
exercises.intensity_cue: Rate execution and effort from 1-10
exercises.form_cue: State one observed cue, one good decision, and one action to improve next time.

source_chapter: 02 Development Program Foundation; 06 Ages & Stages; 07 Training Methodology
progression_rule: Use this routine after a high-load day or when readiness is low. Return to normal training only when movement is pain-free and the player's next-day readiness improves; recovery work should not become another hard session.

exercises.name: Easy Ball Walk and Dribble
exercises.intensity_cue: RPE 2-3 out of 10
exercises.form_cue: Keep the shoulders relaxed and use soft touches with both feet.

exercises.name: Dynamic Mobility Flow
exercises.intensity_cue: Comfortable range with no forced stretch
exercises.form_cue: Move slowly through the hips, ankles, and thoracic spine without bouncing.

exercises.name: Low-Intensity Coordination
exercises.intensity_cue: RPE 3 out of 10
exercises.form_cue: Prioritize smooth rhythm and balance over speed.

exercises.name: Breathing Reset
exercises.intensity_cue: Slow nasal breathing
exercises.form_cue: Use a longer exhale while keeping the ribs stacked over the pelvis.

exercises.name: Readiness Check
exercises.reps_or_duration: Record sleep, soreness, energy, and motivation from 1-5
exercises.intensity_cue: Honest self-report before the next training day
exercises.form_cue: Report pain separately from normal muscle soreness.

source_chapter: 02 Development Program Foundation; 08 Periodization of Te-Ta; 09 Player Selection Criteria
progression_rule: Record completed volume, session minutes, and session RPE after every workout, then calculate session load as minutes multiplied by RPE. Increase the next week's total load by no more than 10% when completion, readiness, and movement quality remain stable; otherwise hold or reduce the load.

exercises.name: Ten-Meter Speed Check
exercises.intensity_cue: Maximum quality after a full warm-up
exercises.form_cue: Use the same start position and surface for every test.

exercises.name: Reactive Agility Check
exercises.reps_or_duration: 1 reaction each direction with 90 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Maximum controlled speed
exercises.form_cue: Record only trials completed without slipping or losing balance.

exercises.name: Two-Foot Passing Accuracy Check
exercises.reps_or_duration: 20 passes per foot with 60 seconds rest
exercises.intensity_cue: Firm pass to a fixed target
exercises.form_cue: Use the same distance and target size at every audit.

exercises.name: Session Load Log
exercises.reps_or_duration: Record completed minutes and RPE 1-10 after each workout
exercises.intensity_cue: Session load equals minutes multiplied by RPE
exercises.form_cue: Log the actual completed work rather than the scheduled work.

exercises.name: Weekly Completion Review
exercises.reps_or_duration: Review completed sets, missed sessions, soreness, and comments once per week
exercises.intensity_cue: Coach reviews before sending the next schedule
exercises.form_cue: Change one training variable at a time so the response can be evaluated.
